worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement was written, signed and within the supervising physician's scope when it was made twenty-six months ago, and it contains individually developed prescriptive guidelines. Neither party has reviewed it since. The pharmacist proposes to keep co-managing referred patients under it while a review is scheduled, on the footing that nothing about the arrangement has changed. Is she right?
steps: Run the constitutive elements first: M.G.L. c. 112, § 24B1/2(a) requires a written and signed agreement between a qualifying pharmacist and a supervising physician, defining a collaborative practice within the scope of the physician's practice. All of those are satisfied on these facts.

Then read the next sentence of the same definition, which is a continuing condition rather than a formation requirement: each collaborative practice agreement shall be subject to review and renewal on a biennial basis.

Confirm the operational statement of the same duty at 247 CMR 16.04(4): a collaborative practice agreement must be reviewed and renewed by the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician or physicians at least every two years.
Measure the interval. Twenty-six months is more than two years, so the review and renewal fell due at some point before month twenty-seven and has not happened.
Note who carries the duty. It sits on the pharmacist and the physician themselves, so no board notice was going to arrive, and a review that is merely scheduled is not a review that has been done.
worked_examples.resolution: The agreement is out of currency, and a pending review does not preserve it. The error the scenario invites is to run the formation checklist, find every element satisfied, and never ask when the instrument was last reviewed and renewed.

worked_examples.scenario: An authorized pharmacist holds two patient referrals. One was completed by the supervising physician in indelible pencil on a paper form. The other arrived by email as a flattened image that the pharmacy system can display once but can neither store nor retrieve afterwards in readable form. The pharmacist assumes the emailed one is the safer of the two because it is electronic and time-stamped. How should each be assessed?
steps: Start from the definition rather than from intuition: 243 CMR 2.12(1) says what written means for collaborative practice agreement referrals, consents and other related documents.

Apply the paper limb. A paper-based document satisfies the requirement if it is written in ink, indelible pencil or any other means, and indelible pencil is named in the regulation itself, so the pencil referral passes.

Apply the electronic limb, which is the conditioned one. The transmission must be in a format that maintains patient confidentiality and that can be read and stored in a retrievable and readable form.

Test the emailed image against that condition. A file the receiving system cannot store or later retrieve in readable form fails the storage and retrievability half of the test, whatever its appearance.

Note the additional conditions the same paragraph places on electronic transmission with electronic signatures: accord with M.G.L. c. 94C, § 23(g), 105 CMR 721.00, and 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a).
worked_examples.resolution: The indelible pencil referral satisfies the writing requirement and the emailed image does not. The error the scenario invites is treating the electronic document as the more compliant one because it looks more formal, when the electronic route is the route that carries conditions.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement names three duties of the authorized pharmacist that may be delegated to appropriately trained staff and two duties that may not be delegated, and says nothing further on the subject. The pharmacist proposes to delegate one of the three named duties to a certified technician for the next six weeks, reasoning that the duty is on the permitted list and the technician is trained. What is still missing?
steps: Read 247 CMR 16.04(3) as two sentences rather than one. The first requires the agreement to specify the delegable duties and the duties that shall not be delegated; the agreement here satisfies that sentence.

Read the second sentence, which is the one the facts are aimed at: the agreement shall specify when and how an authorized pharmacist may delegate duties under the agreement, and the duration and scope of the delegation.

Match the proposal against it. A six-week delegation is a duration, but the duration has to be specified in the agreement rather than chosen afterwards by the pharmacist, and the when, the how and the scope are absent as well.

Resist the argument from competence. The staff member's training is a condition the regulation attaches to a delegation the agreement has authorised, not a substitute for the agreement authorising it.

Keep the ordinary scope rules in view: pharmacy intern and pharmacy technician duties supporting an authorized pharmacist under an agreement must still be performed in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06.
worked_examples.resolution: The agreement still lacks the when and how of delegation together with its duration and scope, so the delegation cannot go ahead on the present terms. The error the scenario invites is stopping at the first sentence of the paragraph and treating the naming of duties as the whole obligation.

worked_examples.scenario: During an inspection an authorized pharmacist produces the signed original agreement, which the supervising physician handed over for safekeeping, and nothing else. Asked for the patient referral and consent, the pharmacist says the physician keeps those. An investigator from the Board of Registration in Medicine then asks to see the file, and the pharmacist answers that the documents are retrievable only to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy. How many things have gone wrong?
steps: Identify what the pharmacist is required to hold under 247 CMR 16.04(6): a copy of the current collaborative practice agreement, including copies of the current patient referral and patient consent, in the primary practice setting.
Test the first answer. Holding the original is not compliance with a requirement to maintain a copy, and it also strips the physician's record of what the physician is required to keep.
Test the second. The referral and consent copies are part of the same obligation, so a file containing the agreement alone is incomplete even if the agreement itself is current.

Test the third. The copy must be readily retrievable at the request of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and the Board of Registration in Medicine, so an answer limited to one board is wrong on its face.

Place the original where it belongs. In accordance with 243 CMR 2.12 the supervising physician must maintain the original of the current agreement, including the original current referral and consent, in the patient's medical record in the physician's own custody, so the transfer for safekeeping was not open to the parties to arrange.
worked_examples.resolution: Three things have gone wrong: the pharmacist holds the original instead of a copy, the referral and consent copies are missing, and retrievability was refused to one of the two boards entitled to ask. The error the scenario invites is treating custody as a housekeeping matter the two professionals may allocate between themselves.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement lapses at the end of this month and will not be renewed. The pharmacist plans to write to each affected patient during the following week, explaining that the arrangement has ended and setting out how the patient's therapy will be continued, and considers that this discharges what is owed. Separately, the pharmacist resolved a Board matter last month by consent agreement that placed a condition on her practice, and she works under agreements with three supervising physicians. What has she missed?
steps: Split 247 CMR 16.04(5) into its two duties. Prior to termination or non-renewal, the pharmacist and the supervising physician shall arrange for an uninterrupted continuation of the patient's drug therapy in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

Read the second duty. When the agreement is not renewed or collaborative drug therapy management is otherwise terminated, the pharmacist and the supervising physician shall inform the patient in writing of the termination and of the procedures in place for continuation of the therapy.

Match the plan to the duties. The planned letter is the second duty and is timed correctly for it, but nothing in the plan is the arrangement for uninterrupted continuation, which was owed before the lapse.
Note that both duties are joint. They are owed by the authorized pharmacist and the supervising physician together, so a plan by the pharmacist alone does not discharge either of them.

Turn to the consent agreement. Under 247 CMR 16.02(3), discipline by the Board whether by agreement or Board order, and any other practice restriction, requires the pharmacist to provide written notification of the discipline or practice restriction to each supervising physician, which on these facts means three notifications rather than one.
worked_examples.resolution: She has missed the pre-termination arrangement for uninterrupted continuation of therapy, and she owes written notification of the consent agreement to each of her three supervising physicians. The error the scenario invites is twofold: seeing a written notice in the plan, matching it to the written-notice duty and stopping; and treating a matter resolved by agreement as something short of discipline.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist completed her collaborative practice continuing education two years ago. Her current collaborative practice agreement was signed six months ago. She proposes to discard the course documentation on the ground that the courses themselves are now more than two years old, and adds that her pharmacist registration has been renewed since. May she?
steps: Locate the retention duty at 247 CMR 16.02(2): an authorized pharmacist participating in collaborative drug therapy management must maintain evidence of completion of required continuing education for at least two years after the date of the current collaborative practice agreement.
Fix the start of the clock. It runs from the date of the current agreement, not from the date of the course and not from any registration renewal.
Apply it. The current agreement is six months old, so the two-year period has eighteen months left to run and every piece of evidence for it is still inside the retention period.

Identify what is being retained: evidence of completion of the continuing education required for participation, which under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e) is at least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education in each year of the term of the agreement.
worked_examples.resolution: She may not discard the documentation; it must be kept for at least two years after the date of the current agreement. The error the scenario invites is measuring the retention period from the course date or from a registration renewal, either of which would release records the regulation still requires.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A collaborative practice agreement is a ______ and ______ agreement between which two parties?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Written and signed, between a pharmacist with training and experience relevant to the scope of the collaborative practice and a supervising physician, under M.G.L. c. 112, § 24B1/2(a) and restated at 247 CMR 16.04(1).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Whose scope of practice limits the collaborative practice an agreement may define?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The supervising physician's. The collaborative practice must be within the scope of the supervising physician's practice, so the agreement cannot reach past it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How often must a collaborative practice agreement be reviewed and renewed, and by whom?
retrieval_prompts.answer: On a biennial basis under the statutory definition; 247 CMR 16.04(4) states it as at least every two years, by the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician or physicians themselves.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does the statutory definition require an agreement to include where the pharmacist is to prescribe?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice of the pharmacist.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a referral written in indelible pencil fails the writing requirement.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 243 CMR 2.12(1)(a) permits a paper-based document written in ink, indelible pencil or any other means, and names indelible pencil expressly.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the two qualities an electronically transmitted collaborative document's format must have.
retrieval_prompts.answer: It must maintain patient confidentiality, and it must be capable of being read and stored in a retrievable and readable form.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which external instruments must an electronic transmission with electronic signatures accord with?
retrieval_prompts.answer: M.G.L. c. 94C, § 23(g); 105 CMR 721.00; and 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a), with the information transmitted without alteration.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: List the four things 247 CMR 16.04(3) requires a collaborative practice agreement to specify about delegation.
retrieval_prompts.answer: The duties that may be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff; the duties that shall not be delegated; when and how the authorized pharmacist may delegate; and the duration and scope of the delegation.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An agreement is silent on delegation. May an appropriately trained technician take on one of the pharmacist's duties?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. Silence is not permission; the agreement must specify the delegable and non-delegable duties and the terms of delegation before any delegation power exists.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which party holds the original of the current agreement, and where must it be kept?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The supervising physician, in the patient's medical record in the physician's own custody, in accordance with 243 CMR 2.12.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What three documents must the authorized pharmacist maintain in the primary practice setting?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A copy of the current collaborative practice agreement, plus copies of the current patient referral and the current patient consent.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: At whose request must the pharmacist's copy be readily retrievable?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Both the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and the Board of Registration in Medicine.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which termination duty is owed before the agreement ends, and which is owed at the ending?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Before: arranging an uninterrupted continuation of the patient's drug therapy. At the ending: informing the patient in writing of the termination and of the continuation procedures. Both are owed jointly and in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Board matter is resolved by consent agreement with a condition on practice. What is owed, and to whom?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Written notification of the discipline or practice restriction to each supervising physician; discipline by agreement counts the same as a Board order.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Evidence of collaborative practice continuing education must be kept for how long, measured from what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least two years, measured from the date of the current collaborative practice agreement, not from the course date.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How many contact hours of continuing education does participation require, and over what period?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education in each year of the term of the agreement, addressing areas of practice generally related to the particular agreement, under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e).

quick_review.text: A collaborative practice agreement is a written and signed agreement between a pharmacist with training and experience relevant to the scope of the collaborative practice and a supervising physician, defining the collaborative practice the two propose to engage in.
The collaborative practice defined by the agreement must be within the scope of the supervising physician's practice.

Each agreement is subject to review and renewal on a biennial basis; 247 CMR 16.04(4) puts the same duty as review and renewal by the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician or physicians at least every two years.
An agreement shall include individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice of the pharmacist.

For collaborative documents, written means, if paper based, written in ink, indelible pencil or any other means; or transmitted electronically in a format that maintains patient confidentiality and can be read and stored in a retrievable and readable form.

Electronic transmission with electronic signatures is permitted without alteration of the information, provided it accords with M.G.L. c. 94C, § 23(g), 105 CMR 721.00, and 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a).
The agreement must specify both the duties of the authorized pharmacist that may be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff and those that shall not be delegated.
The agreement must also specify when and how an authorized pharmacist may delegate duties under it, and the duration and scope of the delegation; naming the duties alone is half the paragraph.
Pharmacy intern and pharmacy technician duties supporting an authorized pharmacist under an agreement must be performed in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06.

The authorized pharmacist maintains a copy of the current agreement, with copies of the current patient referral and patient consent, in the primary practice setting, readily retrievable at the request of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and the Board of Registration in Medicine.
The supervising physician maintains the original of the current agreement, with the original current referral and consent, in the patient's medical record in the physician's custody.

Prior to termination or non-renewal, the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician shall arrange for an uninterrupted continuation of the patient's drug therapy, in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

When an agreement is not renewed or collaborative drug therapy management is otherwise terminated, the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician shall inform the patient in writing of the termination and of the procedures in place for continuation of the therapy.
Discipline by the Board, whether by agreement or Board order, and any other practice restriction, requires the authorized pharmacist to give written notification of it to each supervising physician.
Evidence of completion of required continuing education must be maintained for at least two years after the date of the current collaborative practice agreement.

Participation requires at least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education in each year of the term of the agreement, addressing areas of practice generally related to the particular agreement.

decision_logic.condition: A set of facts asks whether a pharmacist may act under a collaborative practice agreement.
decision_logic.action: Test constitution first, then currency. Constitution: written, signed, the right two parties, and a collaborative practice inside the supervising physician's scope. Currency: reviewed and renewed within the last two years.

decision_logic.condition: The formation elements all check out and the facts give a date for the agreement.
decision_logic.action: Compute the interval since the last review and renewal. More than two years puts the agreement out of currency regardless of how well it was drafted, and a review that is only scheduled does not stop the clock.

decision_logic.condition: The agreement provides for the pharmacist to prescribe.
decision_logic.action: Check that individually developed guidelines for that prescriptive practice are included in the agreement itself; the further conditions attaching to prescriptive practice are treated in a separate section.

decision_logic.condition: A document is challenged as not being in writing.
decision_logic.action: Ask which route it took. If paper based, ink, indelible pencil or any other means will do. If electronic, test confidentiality, readability and storage in a retrievable and readable form, and then the accord with M.G.L. c. 94C, § 23(g), 105 CMR 721.00, and 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a).

decision_logic.condition: Somebody other than the authorized pharmacist is to perform a duty under the agreement.
decision_logic.action: Read the agreement for all four delegation elements before looking at the person. Absent any of them there is no delegation power, and the staff member's training does not create one.

decision_logic.condition: An inspector or investigator asks for the collaborative practice documents.
decision_logic.action: Produce the pharmacist's copy of the current agreement together with copies of the current referral and consent, from the primary practice setting, and produce them for the Board of Registration in Medicine as readily as for the Board of Registration in Pharmacy.

decision_logic.condition: A physician offers to leave the original agreement, referral or consent with the pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Decline the transfer. The original of each belongs in the patient's medical record in the custody of the supervising physician, and the pharmacist's obligation is discharged by a copy.

decision_logic.condition: An agreement is about to lapse, or either party proposes to end it.
decision_logic.action: Do the continuity work first, before the ending, jointly with the other party and on the terms the agreement itself sets; then, at the ending, send the patient a written notice covering both the termination and the continuation procedures.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist in collaborative practice is disciplined or has any restriction placed on practice.
decision_logic.action: Count the supervising physicians and send each one a written notification of the discipline or practice restriction; a consent agreement is not an exemption, and neither is a restriction imposed outside a formal disciplinary process.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist is deciding whether continuing education records may be destroyed.
decision_logic.action: Take the date of the current collaborative practice agreement, add two years, and keep everything until that date has passed; the course date and the registration renewal date are irrelevant to this calculation.

exceptions.text: The individually developed guidelines element of the statutory definition is conditioned on there being prescriptive practice: the agreement shall include individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice of the pharmacist, so an agreement with no prescriptive component is not defective for lacking them.

247 CMR 16.04(3) does not displace the ordinary scope rules for support staff. Pharmacy intern and pharmacy technician duties providing support to an authorized pharmacist acting under an agreement must still be performed in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01 for interns and 8.02 through 8.06 for technicians, so an agreement term cannot enlarge what those roles may do.

The writing definition is expressed as two alternatives rather than a single standard: a document satisfies it either by the paper route or by the electronic route, and failing the conditions attached to the electronic route does not convert the document into a compliant paper one.

timing_deadlines.event: Review and renewal of a collaborative practice agreement
timing_deadlines.timeframe: On a biennial basis; 247 CMR 16.04(4) states it as at least every two years
timing_deadlines.consequence: An agreement not reviewed and renewed within the period is no longer current, whatever its contents provide

timing_deadlines.event: Board-approved continuing education for collaborative practice
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least five additional contact hours in each year of the term of the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: The continuing education required for participation is unmet, and there is nothing for the retention duty to preserve

timing_deadlines.event: Retention of evidence of completion of required continuing education
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least two years after the date of the current collaborative practice agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: Records discarded before that date are discarded early, even if the courses themselves are older than two years

timing_deadlines.event: Arranging an uninterrupted continuation of the patient's drug therapy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Prior to termination or non-renewal of the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: A duty owed before the ending is missed, and no notice sent afterwards repairs it

timing_deadlines.event: Written notice to the patient of termination and of the continuation procedures
timing_deadlines.timeframe: When the agreement is not renewed, or collaborative drug therapy management is otherwise terminated
timing_deadlines.consequence: The patient is left without the written statement of the termination and of the arrangements now in place

timing_deadlines.event: Written notification of discipline or a practice restriction to each supervising physician
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Whenever the pharmacist is disciplined by the Board, whether by agreement or Board order, or is otherwise subject to any practice restriction
timing_deadlines.consequence: Each supervising physician not notified is a physician supervising in ignorance of a restriction on the pharmacist's practice

timing_deadlines.event: Production of the pharmacist's copy of the agreement, referral and consent
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Readily retrievable at the request of either board; the regulation sets a standard of retrievability rather than a period
timing_deadlines.consequence: A file that has to be assembled or fetched from elsewhere is not readily retrievable in the primary practice setting

timing_deadlines.event: Currency of the copies held by the pharmacist
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Continuously, for as long as the pharmacist acts under the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: A superseded agreement, referral or consent on file does not satisfy a requirement expressed in terms of the current documents

forms_records.text: The agreement itself: a written and signed instrument naming a pharmacist with training and experience relevant to the scope of the collaborative practice and a supervising physician, and defining the collaborative practice the two propose to engage in.
Where the agreement provides for the pharmacist to prescribe, it must carry individually developed guidelines for that prescriptive practice on its face.
A paper-based agreement, referral, consent or related document may be written in ink, indelible pencil or any other means.

An electronic agreement, referral, consent or related document must be in a format that maintains patient confidentiality and can be read and stored in a retrievable and readable form, may carry electronic signatures, must be transmitted without alteration of the information, and must accord with M.G.L. c. 94C, § 23(g), 105 CMR 721.00, and 247 CMR 9.01(19) and 9.07(1)(a).

The delegation terms are part of the agreement's own text: the delegable duties, the duties that shall not be delegated, when and how delegation may occur, and the duration and scope of the delegation.

The pharmacist's file in the primary practice setting: a copy of the current agreement, a copy of the current patient referral and a copy of the current patient consent, held so as to be readily retrievable at the request of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and the Board of Registration in Medicine.

The physician's file: the original of the current agreement, together with the original current patient referral and patient consent, in the patient's medical record in the custody of the supervising physician.
The written notice to the patient on termination or non-renewal states two things, the termination itself and the procedures in place for the continuation of the patient's drug therapy.

The written notification of discipline or practice restriction is a separate document owed to each supervising physician, and its trigger is the discipline or restriction rather than anything happening to the agreement.
Evidence of completion of the required continuing education is retained by the pharmacist for at least two years after the date of the current collaborative practice agreement.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist, as a party to the agreement
role_duties.duty: Enter only into a written and signed agreement whose defined collaborative practice sits inside the supervising physician's scope, and take part in reviewing and renewing it at least every two years.

role_duties.role: Supervising physician, as a party to the agreement
role_duties.duty: Confine the collaborative practice the agreement defines to the scope of the physician's own practice, and take part in the biennial review and renewal.

role_duties.role: Either party preparing a collaborative document
role_duties.duty: Produce it either on paper in ink, indelible pencil or any other means, or electronically in a confidential format that can be read and stored in a retrievable and readable form and that accords with the instruments 243 CMR 2.12(1)(b) names.

role_duties.role: Drafter of the agreement
role_duties.duty: State the delegable duties, the duties that shall not be delegated, and when, how, for how long and how widely the authorized pharmacist may delegate.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist proposing to delegate
role_duties.duty: Act only within delegation terms the agreement already contains, and only to appropriately trained and authorized staff, with intern and technician support kept inside 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist, as custodian
role_duties.duty: Maintain a copy of the current agreement with copies of the current referral and consent in the primary practice setting, readily retrievable at the request of either board.

role_duties.role: Supervising physician, as custodian
role_duties.duty: Maintain the original of the current agreement with the original current referral and consent in the patient's medical record in the physician's own custody.

role_duties.role: Board of Registration in Pharmacy and Board of Registration in Medicine
role_duties.duty: Either board may request the pharmacist's copy of the agreement, referral and consent, and the retrievability obligation runs to both of them equally.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist and supervising physician, jointly, before an agreement ends
role_duties.duty: Arrange for an uninterrupted continuation of the patient's drug therapy, in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist and supervising physician, jointly, at the ending
role_duties.duty: Inform the patient in writing of the termination and of the procedures in place for the continuation of the patient's drug therapy.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist who has been disciplined or restricted
role_duties.duty: Give written notification of the discipline or practice restriction to each supervising physician, counting consent agreements as discipline.

role_duties.role: Authorized pharmacist, as keeper of continuing education evidence
role_duties.duty: Complete at least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education in each year of the term of the agreement and retain the evidence for at least two years after the date of the current agreement.

common_traps.text: Running the formation checklist, finding every element satisfied, and never asking when the agreement was last reviewed and renewed. Constitution and currency are separate tests and the second is the one that lapses quietly.
Adding a board filing step. Nothing in the definition makes the agreement effective on filing with a board; the filing the regulations require is filing a copy in the primary practice setting.

Reading the physician-scope limit as a formality. An agreement that defines a collaborative practice outside the supervising physician's own scope is defective in its definition, not merely ambitious.
Assuming the electronic document is the more compliant one because it looks more formal. The paper route carries almost no conditions and the electronic route carries all of them.
Rejecting indelible pencil as too informal, when the regulation names it in the same breath as ink.
Stopping after the first sentence of 247 CMR 16.04(3). Naming the delegable and non-delegable duties is half the paragraph; the when, the how, the duration and the scope are the other half.

Reasoning from the competence of the staff member rather than from the content of the agreement. Training is a condition on a delegation the agreement has authorised, not a source of authority in itself.
Holding the signed original on site and treating that as the more careful course. The pharmacist's obligation is to hold a copy, and the original belongs in the physician's record.
Producing the agreement without the referral and consent copies, or treating retrievability as owed to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy alone.
Collapsing the two termination duties into one notification after the ending. The continuity arrangement is owed before termination or non-renewal and is not discharged by any letter.
Assuming oral notice to the patient will do, or that the duties fall on the physician alone. The notice must be in writing and both duties are owed jointly.
Treating a matter resolved by consent agreement as something short of discipline, or notifying only the physician whose agreement relates to the conduct at issue.
Measuring the continuing education retention period from the course date or from the pharmacist's registration renewal instead of from the date of the current collaborative practice agreement.

orientation.text: Massachusetts locates a pharmacist's prescribing authority in 105 CMR 700.003, the Department of Public Health section on registration of persons for a specific activity, and the paragraph that carries the authority is 105 CMR 700.003(G). Its opening words are the whole of the power: a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, provided the following requirements are met. Two things follow from that single sentence and both are examinable. The power is three-fold, and the words as authorized in attach to each of the three acts separately rather than to the bundle. And the sentence closes on a proviso, so the numbered paragraphs that follow are not commentary on the power; they are conditions on it, and a pharmacist who fails one of them is not a pharmacist exercising a power imperfectly but a pharmacist without the power at all.

Read the three acts as three separate permissions. Issuing starts a prescription or medication order. Modifying changes one that already exists. Discontinuing stops the therapy. Nothing in the opening words ranks them by gravity, and nothing makes the smaller act a component of the larger one, so the intuition that a pharmacist trusted to change a dose must also be trusted to stop the drug has no foothold in the text. Discontinuation in particular is a regulated prescribing act and not a clinical judgement sitting outside the regulation, which is why an agreement silent on discontinuation leaves the pharmacist without authority to discontinue no matter how plainly the clinical case for stopping is made out. The other half of the opening words does comparable work on the agreement itself: the agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, three named instruments read conjunctively, so an agreement answering one of them but not the others is not an agreement this paragraph recognises.

The first of the conditions this section teaches is 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2): the pharmacist registers with the Department, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000. The load-bearing words are for the purpose of prescribing. A pharmacist may already hold a Department controlled substance registration obtained for some other activity, and the paragraph declines to treat a registration as one undifferentiated permission to handle controlled substances: the purpose for which the registration was taken out is part of the requirement, so a registration obtained so that a pharmacy could dispense does not carry prescribing authority across to a collaborating pharmacist. The federal limb is drafted differently again. It is expressly conditional, the pharmacist registering with the DEA if applicable, so it does not attach to every collaborating pharmacist merely because an agreement exists; and the regulation refers the question of when it does apply out to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 rather than answering it in its own terms, which means the answer turns on what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

A second registration requirement comes from the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and is easily conflated with the first. 247 CMR 16.02(1) sets out the qualifications a pharmacist must satisfy to enter into a collaborative practice agreement and engage in collaborative practice, and 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) adds three further conditions, but only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement. The first is to maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000. The second is to complete training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) prior to initially obtaining a controlled substance registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence. The third is to submit an attestation, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth, in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Notice what each condition is fastened to, because that is where the examinable difference sits: the registration to the term of the agreement, the training to the renewal of the pharmacist licence, and the attestation to a state of affairs the pharmacist swears to. The other qualifications listed in 247 CMR 16.02(1) apply to every collaborating pharmacist and belong to the companion section on who may practise; only subparagraph (f) is triggered by prescriptive practices.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) governs what happens when the prescription leaves the prescribing pharmacist and reaches someone who will fill it. The pharmacist may issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20, which is the general law's oral prescription provision, provided that the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies their name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides their registration number, work address, phone number, and the name of the supervising physician. Two things are clearly identified and four things are provided, and every one of the six runs to the dispensing pharmacist rather than to the patient, which is what a transmission between two pharmacists looks like. Three of the four provided particulars are the sort of thing any prescriber supplies. The work address is stated as a work address, so a home address or a mobile number offered in its place does not answer the paragraph. The distinctive particular is the last one, the name of the supervising physician, which an ordinary practitioner prescription never carries and which the pharmacist's own prescribing authority does not dispense with. Because these particulars are the proviso on which the pharmacist may issue at all, a transmission that omits one of them is incomplete rather than merely untidy, and the course open to the receiving pharmacist is to obtain the missing particular before filling rather than to weigh how material it seemed.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) deals with the opposite situation, a patient who will not be carrying a prescription to a pharmacy because the patient is inside a licensed health facility. There the pharmacist may prescribe a controlled substance for the patient through the use of a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided that such a written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000. Three elements decide questions on this paragraph. The instrument is a written medication order, not an outpatient prescription form and not an oral instruction. The place is the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, not a record the pharmacy or the pharmacist keeps and not a note left with staff. And the gate is that the facility is a licensed health facility; the paragraph names a hospital, a long term care facility, an ambulatory care clinic and a hospice, introducing them with the word including, so those four are an illustration of the class rather than the class itself, and a setting that holds no health facility licence falls outside the paragraph however carefully it maintains care records of its own.

This section is the prescribing act and nothing more. It does not decide what collaborative drug therapy management is or who may enter into an agreement, and it does not decide what the agreement document must contain; those are the subjects of the companion sections on the practice and on the agreement, and a question about qualifications, referral, consent or required agreement terms is answered there. It also stops short of the retail regime. 105 CMR 700.003(G) addresses particular settings in separate numbered paragraphs, of which the facility paragraph taught here is one, and the paragraph directed at the retail setting, together with the statutory conditions on a collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business and the schedules such a pharmacist may or may not be authorised to prescribe, is the retail section's material. Where a question turns on what a pharmacist practising in a community or retail pharmacy may prescribe, this section supplies the power, the registration and the instrument, and the schedule limits must be taken from the retail section rather than inferred from anything here.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement authorises a pharmacist to issue prescriptions for a referred patient's hypertension and to discontinue therapy where a listed adverse effect appears. It says nothing about changing doses. Reviewing the patient, the pharmacist concludes that the current dose should be halved rather than stopped. May she halve it?
steps: Return to the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G): a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement.
Separate the three acts. This agreement addresses issuing and discontinuing, and modifying is a distinct act rather than a lesser instance of either of them.
Resist the direction of travel in the facts. Halving a dose looks more conservative than stopping the drug, but conservatism is not the test the paragraph applies; authorisation act by act is.
Check the remaining route. Discontinuation is authorised, so stopping the drug is within the agreement, but that does not convert into a power to leave the patient on a changed dose.
worked_examples.resolution: She may not modify the dose under this agreement. The error the scenario invites is ranking the three acts by clinical gravity and assuming authority to do the graver act carries authority to do the milder one; the opening words authorise each act only as authorized in the agreement, so the agreement has to be amended before she can modify.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist holds a current Department controlled substance registration that her employer obtained years ago so that the pharmacy could dispense. She now signs a collaborative practice agreement that includes prescriptive practices and proposes to prescribe. She reasons that a controlled substance registration is a controlled substance registration. What is missing?
steps: Read 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) as a whole: the pharmacist registers with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
Test her registration against the purpose element rather than against its currency. It is current, but it was obtained for dispensing, and the purpose is part of the requirement.

Now add the Board's overlay, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

Keep the two registration requirements apart. One is a condition on the prescribing power in the Department's regulation; the other is a qualification in the Board's regulation that runs for the term of the agreement.
worked_examples.resolution: She needs Department registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices, the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) as well. The error the scenario invites is treating a controlled substance registration as one undifferentiated permission, so that an instrument held for another purpose is read as covering this one.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist telephones a prescription to a pharmacy across town. She gives her name, says she is a pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement, gives her registration number, names her supervising physician, and offers her mobile number, saying she moves between sites and has no fixed work address to give. The receiving pharmacist is minded to fill it.
steps: List what 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) requires: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, and registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician provided.
Mark off what was supplied. Name, designation, registration number, supervising physician and a phone number are all present.
Identify what is absent. The paragraph specifies a work address as a particular in its own right, alongside the phone number, so a contact number does not stand in for it.
Treat the proviso as a condition on issuing rather than as a checklist of good practice, which means the transmission is incomplete as it stands.
worked_examples.resolution: The receiving pharmacist should obtain the work address before filling. The error the scenario invites is substituting one particular for another on the reasoning that the prescriber is reachable anyway, when the paragraph lists the work address and the phone number as separate items and conditions the pharmacist's power to issue on all of them being supplied.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist prescribes a controlled substance for a patient of a licensed hospice under an agreement that authorises her to do so. She writes a medication order rather than a prescription, but files it in the collaborative practice file her pharmacy department keeps for the hospice, and tells the hospice nurse the order is on file. Has she used the paragraph correctly?
steps: Confirm the setting first. A hospice is among the licensed health facilities 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) names, so the paragraph is available to her.
Confirm the instrument. She wrote a medication order rather than an outpatient prescription form, which is what the paragraph calls for.
Test the location of the writing, which is the element she has got wrong: the paragraph requires the written medication order to be entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.
Note the closing condition as well, that such a written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000, so getting the instrument right does not exhaust the paragraph.
worked_examples.resolution: She has used the right instrument in the right kind of setting but has entered it in the wrong record, so the paragraph is not satisfied until the order is entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the hospice. The error the scenario invites is treating the medication order as a document the pharmacy owns and files, when the paragraph fixes both the instrument and the record it must live on.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist practises under an agreement at a licensed ambulatory care clinic, where she prescribes for referred patients by medication order. One patient is leaving the clinic and needs the same therapy dispensed by a community pharmacy near home. The pharmacist proposes to write the same medication order and let the patient take a copy to that pharmacy. What has to change, and what cannot be decided from this section?
steps: Separate the two instruments. Inside the clinic, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.

Recognise that a prescription reaching a pharmacy for dispensing is the subject of a different paragraph, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), which permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20.

Attach the particulars to the second route: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, plus registration number, work address, phone number and the supervising physician's name.

Stop before the question this section does not answer. Whether a pharmacist may prescribe this particular product for dispensing in a community or retail pharmacy depends on the separate retail regime, which is the companion section's subject.
worked_examples.resolution: The instrument must change: a facility medication order does not travel, and issuing to a dispensing pharmacy engages 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) and its particulars. The error the scenario invites is carrying an instrument that worked in one setting into another, and the further trap is trying to settle the schedule question here rather than in the retail section.

quick_review.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G) opens by permitting a pharmacist to issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement, and closes on the words provided the following requirements are met.
Each of the three acts must be found in the agreement separately; the acts are stated in parallel, so none of them implies another.
The agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 together, not one of them at the drafter's choice.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and with the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
A Department registration obtained for a different activity does not carry prescribing authority, because the purpose forms part of the requirement.
The DEA limb is qualified by the words if applicable, so it binds according to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 and not by virtue of the collaborative practice agreement.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) attaches three conditions, and only where prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement.

Those conditions are a Department controlled substance registration maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and a sworn MassHealth attestation.
The section 18(e) training is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, which ties a prescriptive-practice condition to the licence rather than to the agreement.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 provided the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.
The particulars in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) run to the dispensing pharmacist, and the work address is listed separately from the phone number.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility through a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided the order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist proposes to act on a patient's drug therapy under a collaborative practice agreement.
decision_logic.action: Name the act first: issuing, modifying or discontinuing. Then look for that act, by name, in the agreement, because 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorises each one only as authorized in the agreement.

decision_logic.condition: The agreement authorises the act, and the question is whether the pharmacist may exercise the power at all.
decision_logic.action: Treat the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as conditions, since the opening words end provided the following requirements are met, and work through the ones that bear on the facts.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacist already holds a Department controlled substance registration.
decision_logic.action: Ask what purpose it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, so a registration held for another activity does not satisfy it.

decision_logic.condition: A question asks whether the collaborating pharmacist needs DEA registration.
decision_logic.action: Do not answer yes or no on the strength of the agreement. The limb applies if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, so ask what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

decision_logic.condition: The agreement includes prescriptive practices.
decision_logic.action: Add the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f): the controlled substance registration maintained during the term, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

decision_logic.condition: The prescription is being transmitted to a pharmacist who will dispense it.
decision_logic.action: Check the transmission against the list in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) item by item, and where a particular is missing, obtain it rather than assess how material it was.

decision_logic.condition: The patient is in a facility.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the facility is a licensed health facility. If it is, use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8); if it is not, that paragraph does not supply the instrument.

decision_logic.condition: The question turns on which schedules a pharmacist in a community or retail pharmacy may prescribe.
decision_logic.action: Stop. This section supplies the power, the registration and the instrument; the retail regime and its controlled substance limits are the retail section's material.

ma_vs_federal.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) makes a federal registration part of a Massachusetts condition: the pharmacist registers with the Department and with the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300. Massachusetts therefore treats the federal registration as one of the conditions on its own prescribing power rather than leaving it to federal enforcement alone.

The federal limb is incorporated conditionally. The regulation does not itself state when DEA registration is applicable; it refers that question to 21 CFR 1300, so the Massachusetts requirement is as wide, and no wider, as the federal scheme makes it.

exceptions.text: The DEA limb of 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) applies only if applicable, so it is not a universal precondition of prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement.

The three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) bite only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement; an agreement without prescriptive practices does not attract them.

The medication order route in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) is available only where the patient is in a licensed health facility, so the instrument it authorises is unavailable in a setting that holds no such licence.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacist exercises the prescribing power under a collaborative practice agreement
timing_deadlines.timeframe: The Department registration must be held, for the purpose of prescribing, at the time the power is exercised
timing_deadlines.consequence: Without a registration taken out for that purpose the condition in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is unmet and the power in 105 CMR 700.003(G) is not available.

timing_deadlines.event: Agreement including prescriptive practices is in force
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Throughout the term of the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained for the whole term, so allowing it to lapse mid-term breaks the qualification.

timing_deadlines.event: Training required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Before initially obtaining the controlled substance registration, and at least biennially thereafter
timing_deadlines.consequence: Completion is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2., so the consequence of missing it falls on the licence and not only on the agreement.

forms_records.text: The collaborative practice agreement is the instrument that authorises the prescribing act, and it must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Each of issuing, modifying and discontinuing must appear in it before the pharmacist may do that thing.

A Department registration obtained in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000 is the instrument 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires; the purpose recorded for it is part of what makes it sufficient.
A DEA registration in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 is required by the same paragraph where the federal limb is applicable.

Where prescriptive practices are included, a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department, held pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000, must be maintained during the term of the agreement.

Where prescriptive practices are included, the pharmacist submits an attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

A prescription issued under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) is issued in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 and carries with it, to the dispensing pharmacist, the prescribing pharmacist's name and professional designation, registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

For a patient in a licensed health facility the instrument is a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and that written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement
role_duties.duty: Exercise only those of the three acts, issuing, modifying and discontinuing, that the agreement authorises, and treat the numbered requirements in 105 CMR 700.003(G) as conditions on the power rather than as guidance.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist seeking to prescribe under 105 CMR 700.003(G)
role_duties.duty: Register with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and with the DEA in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 where that limb is applicable.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist whose agreement includes prescriptive practices
role_duties.duty: Maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department for the whole term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist obtaining or renewing a controlled substance registration for prescriptive practice
role_duties.duty: Complete the training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) before initially obtaining the registration and at least biennially thereafter, this being a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist attesting under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)3.
role_duties.duty: Submit the MassHealth participation attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, the attestation covering either participation as a provider of services or the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

role_duties.role: Prescribing pharmacist transmitting a prescription for another pharmacy to fill
role_duties.duty: Clearly identify name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provide registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

role_duties.role: Dispensing pharmacist receiving a prescription from a collaborating pharmacist
role_duties.duty: Check the transmission against the particulars 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) lists, and where one is missing, obtain it, since the particulars are the proviso on which the prescribing pharmacist may issue at all.

role_duties.role: Supervising physician under the agreement
role_duties.duty: Be identified by name in the particulars the prescribing pharmacist supplies to the dispensing pharmacist, so the physician's identity travels with each prescription the pharmacist issues under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7).

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility
role_duties.duty: Use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and make sure that written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

common_traps.text: Ranking issuing, modifying and discontinuing by clinical gravity and assuming the greater authority includes the lesser. The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) state the three acts in parallel and authorise each one only as authorized in the agreement.
Treating a decision to stop a therapy as a clinical judgement outside the regulation. Discontinuation is one of the three regulated prescribing acts.
Reading the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as descriptive detail. The opening sentence ends provided the following requirements are met, which makes them conditions.
Accepting an existing controlled substance registration whatever it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing.
Applying the DEA limb uniformly, either requiring it of every collaborating pharmacist or dismissing it as boilerplate. It is qualified by the words if applicable and points to 21 CFR 1300.

Merging the two registration requirements. The Department registration in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is a condition on the prescribing power; the controlled substance registration in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. is a qualification that must be maintained for the term of the agreement.

Attaching the section 18(e) training to the agreement. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2. makes it a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, and it is required before the registration is first obtained as well as at least biennially thereafter.

Supplying the particulars an ordinary prescriber would give and omitting the supervising physician's name, or offering a callback number in place of the work address. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) lists both, separately.

Writing an outpatient prescription for a facility inpatient, or entering the medication order on a record the pharmacy keeps. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) fixes both the instrument and the record it must be entered on.
Transplanting the facility medication order into a setting that holds no health facility licence because its records look similar. The paragraph is framed for a patient in a licensed health facility.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacist may ISSUE, MODIFY OR DISCONTINUE a prescription or medication order AS AUTHORIZED IN a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. The power is three-fold and each of the three acts must be authorised by the agreement itself, so an agreement that authorises one does not by implication authorise the others.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist registers with the Department, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and with the DEA IF APPLICABLE in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, FOR THE PURPOSE OF PRESCRIBING under 105 CMR 700.000. The purpose of the registration is part of the requirement, so a registration obtained for dispensing does not carry prescribing authority, and the federal limb bites only where it is applicable.
exceptions: The DEA limb applies only if applicable

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f), if prescriptive practices are included in a collaborative practice agreement the pharmacist must maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, §§ 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000; complete the training required under M.G.L. c. 94C, § 18(e) before initially obtaining that controlled substance registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence; and submit an attestation, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, that the pharmacist participates in, or has applied to participate in, MassHealth either as a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist may prescribe a controlled substance for a patient IN A LICENSED HEALTH FACILITY, including a hospital, long term care facility, ambulatory care clinic or hospice, THROUGH THE USE OF A WRITTEN MEDICATION ORDER ENTERED ON THE PATIENT'S MEDICAL RECORD MAINTAINED AT THE FACILITY, provided that such a written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.
